title: Refill Injected root error identity survives for S3 multipart writer terminal close

payload.validation_scope: S3 Storage.Create with concurrency=1 multipart writer: first part upload succeeds, second UploadPart returns an injected root error, then Close is called. Current master completes the upload with only the successful prefix part and returns nil; minimal local fix aborts and returns the injected root error.
payload.user_symptom: A failed large external S3 write can leave a successfully completed partial object when cleanup Close runs after an UploadPart error. The caller may still see the earlier write error, but remote storage state violates failed-write terminal semantics and can leak or publish a truncated object.
payload.scope_caveat: Validated for pkg/objstore/s3store multipart writer and Storage.Create buffered entry. Similar source shape exists in ossstore and ks3, but those are follow-up targets until separately executed.

provenance.source: AI-native refill from issue48164 broad oracle on current master

name: S3 multipart writer must not complete after a failed part upload

payload.p_check: Storage.Create or s3Client.MultipartWriter starts a multipart upload; at least one part upload succeeds and a later UploadPart returns a chosen root error; Close is called afterward by normal cleanup/finalization code.
payload.q_claim: After any UploadPart failure, terminal Close must not call CompleteMultipartUpload for the partial prefix object. It should abort the multipart upload when possible and return an error preserving the injected root cause.
payload.fault_model: Inject a deterministic UploadPart error after one successful prefix part and before Close.

boundary.before: UploadPart returns the chosen root error for part 2
boundary.after: Close terminal behavior: Abort vs Complete call and caller-facing Close error

source_anchors: pkg/objstore/s3store/client.go:415-435 current Write returns UploadPart error but previously did not remember failed state
pkg/objstore/s3store/client.go:445-466 current local fix aborts when failed state exists; vulnerable current master went directly to CompleteMultipartUpload
pkg/objstore/s3like/store.go:618-643 Storage.Create wraps MultipartWriter in objectio.NewBufferedWriter for the user-facing storage writer
pkg/objstore/objectio/writer.go:124-135 BufferedWriter.Close flushes remaining data then calls the underlying writer Close
payload.stop_rule: Record INVALID(harness), not GREEN, if the first part was not uploaded successfully, the injected UploadPart error did not occur, or Close was not executed after the failed write.
payload.scope_caveat: This is not the same obligation as historical issue48164's concurrent io.Pipe overwrite. It is a new terminal-state obligation derived from the same broad error-identity selector.

provenance.source: source-derived P/Q/F plus mock S3 execution

name: S3 multipart failed part is terminal: no Complete and root error survives

payload.contract: For an S3 multipart upload writer, once UploadPart returns a root error, Close must not make the partial upload visible via CompleteMultipartUpload and the terminal Close result must preserve that root error.
payload.narrows: Scoped to S3 multipart writer failed part followed by Close; observes both final error identity and remote-state API action.
red_signature: Close returns nil after an UploadPart error
Close calls CompleteMultipartUpload after an UploadPart error
CompleteMultipartUpload contains only a successful prefix part after a later failed part
Close error does not contain the injected root error
invalid_signature: no prefix part succeeded before the injected failure
mock does not observe Complete or Abort

name: S3 UploadPart error after one successful prefix part

trigger_condition.operation: S3 multipart writer via s3Client.MultipartWriter or Storage.Create with Concurrency=1
trigger_condition.phase: after CreateMultipartUpload and after part 1 UploadPart succeeds
trigger_condition.required_evidence: part 1 UploadPart called and returned an ETag; part 2 UploadPart returned the injected root error

payload.fault_action: Return a deterministic root error from UploadPart for part 2, then call Close on the writer.
payload.observer_action: Count CompleteMultipartUpload and AbortMultipartUpload calls, inspect CompletedMultipartUpload.Parts length, and inspect Close error text/cause.
invalid_if: the test exercises the concurrent uploader path instead of the multipart writer path

lessons.selector_worked: ERROR_IDENTITY_PRESERVATION found a second S3 bug by looking for P: root failure happened, Q: terminal path must still respect it, F: failed state was not stored before a fast terminal Close path.
lessons.quality: This is stronger than a pure error-text bug because the oracle also observes remote-state intent: current master calls CompleteMultipartUpload for a prefix-only partial object after a later part failed.
lessons.method_note: The broad oracle was too vague; the useful refinement was to add a state/action observer, not only final error text.

lessons.fix_shape: Store the first UploadPart error in the multipart writer. Once failed, Close chooses AbortMultipartUpload and returns the stored root error instead of CompleteMultipartUpload.
lessons.package_test_note: A full pkg/objstore/s3store run was attempted but failed in pre-existing retry/read tests unrelated to this oracle; narrow RED/GREEN tests passed.

rationale: the oracle observes both root error preservation and the absence of CompleteMultipartUpload after a failed part
the fault lands after one successful prefix part, which exposes partial-object completion
the terminal Close path after a writer failure is the critical schedule
the broad injected-error oracle becomes actionable only after adding remote-state observers for Complete vs Abort
